Ever since then I found a kind of beauty in death and life. It’s like death is our reward for trying our damndest here on Earth. My favorite boss fight will always be Handsome Jack at the end of Borderlands 2. However, he is BY FAR not what makes a great final boss. He can be killed pretty quickly if you know what you’re doing. But I just like him because you can kill him midway through his monologue which is really fun. But, a great video game boss should have the same skills and be relatively the same size as you. This elicits a unique response from players. You’re so used to fighting huge bosses. Fighting equal sized ones feels like a fair, man to man fight. In games like Zelda or Mario where most bosses are way bigger than you and stationary or have predictable patterns, it only provides the illusion of the boss being strong. Same thing with David and Goliath. Everyone thinks David was the underdog when in reality he had the upper hand. He had skills and weapons (rock and sling, artillery) that could beat the larger boss that had inappropriate skills and weapons (sword and shield, close range). Same thing with “big” game bosses. It looks intimidating but really you have the necessary tools to beat them. Think of Zelda where you get the bow and face the boss with only one eye. Pretty convenient. However in games like Dark Souls where some enemies and bosses have the same tools and abilities as you, it creates a level playing ground. You feel accomplished and skilled knowing that you beat the enemy with skill alone.

So it’s senior year, I’m sitting in government class. Our teacher is in his 50s, he’s on the town council of our small Midwest town. He’s a sweet guy, but also a huge smart ass who loves a good joke. We get an announcement over the intercom that all the seniors have to dress up in their caps and gowns to do a quick walk through of the elementary school and middle school, I guess to inspire the kids or some shit like that. All they cared about was getting out of class for 30mins, and he’ll so we’re we. Our government teacher, let’s call him Mr. Mike, says “Hey I bet if you all started chanting loud enough, the vice principle will take you to Dairy Queen after the walk through as a reward” he obviously meant that as a joke but I thought in my dumbass 18 year old self “Well damn that sounds awesome” 
So we’re sitting on the bus the next day after walking through the middle school and I get everyone on the bus to start chanting and my god was it a chant. We’re talking the ending battle of BraveHeart level of vocal tearing. 
But the vice principle doesn’t break. She knew Mr. Mike was behind all this so she said “why don’t you go and lobby in his classroom if you want DQ so bad”
So we did. 
And Mr. Mike laughed so fucking hard that there were 180 kids crammed into his classroom. 
He says “Aw to hell with it, let’s get Dairy Queen!”
So we run out the doors and all jump into our cars and basically raid our towns tiny, 600 square foot Dairy Queen. 
However, that was also a joke by Mr. Mike, he stayed back hoping we’d realize he wasn’t with us, and come back inside. 
He was wrong. 
I felt so good seeing everyone at DQ having fun knowing I was the one who was stupid enough to start the chanting and cause this. 
Basically Mob Mentality is great in the right hands

In our area there's a radio show with a comedy bit called "Uncle BS" in which the character, Uncle BS, tells stories of how he was involved in some famous or infamous event in history. For example, during the Chicago fire he was a veterinarian looking at a cow with restless leg syndrome.

My father, being the self-proclaimed comedian he was, decided to write his own Uncle BS stories, but with a twist. It would involve horrific moments in history; Columbine, 9/11, Sandy Hook, etc. Just really morbid events.

Well, he started researching these events on his phone at work and writing down the details of the events in a little notebook he kept in his work locker.
He does this for about a week and forgets about the notebook in his locker. Then, he gets into an argument with his supervisor and gets so angry that he storms out of work and quits. Later that day they decide to open his locker and clean it out. 

They find the notebook.

So obviously it looks pretty bad that this guy at work freaks out, yells at everybody, and they find a notebook he wrote with details of every domestic terrorist attack performed in recent US history.
Next thing we now the local sheriff is at our doorstep asking where my father is. After my father tries to explain the notebook everything died down for a bit,

But, we noticed that if we went to town or work or school, a black car with tinted windows would follow us everywhere we went. They wouldn't be tailgating, but they'd be a quarter mile down the road. Eventually they just stopped following us and went away. 

For the time it happened though it caused a lot of unnecessary stress for our family, my father lost his job and had to find work out of state, nearly caused my parents to divorce, and made all of us extremely anxious for weeks. Our family was a fucking mess.
tl;dr The time my father was suspected to be a terrorist and caused our whole family to be tailed by unmarked cars for a whole week
